name: lelwel
description: LL(1) parser generator with a focus on error recovery and lossless output

license.comment: Cargo.toml: `MIT OR Apache-2.0`; repo ships LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE.

approach.comment: Grammar lives in an external `.llw` file compiled via `lelwel::build("src/grammar.llw")` from build.rs into readable recursive-descent Rust code (generated.rs in OUT_DIR).

implementation.comment: Generator deps are logos, codespan-reporting, rustc-hash (all pure Rust); generated parser is plain Rust source. Not verified with `cargo tree`.

documentation.comment: No book; the README's grammar-specification section is the de-facto user guide. docs.rs reports only ~12% of items documented.

grammar-class.comment: LL(1) core with extensions: direct left recursion (Pratt), semantic predicates for arbitrary lookahead, and a restricted ordered choice. Author deliberately avoids GLR/GLL/ALL(*) to keep linear runtime.

grammar-definition.comment: `.llw` grammar file; LSP (`lelwel-ls`) and CLI (`llw`) validate it.

left-recursion.comment: Direct left recursion is written as-is in the grammar; the generator lowers it to a Pratt parser (branch order = binding power, `right` declarations for right-assoc). Indirect left recursion is not supported.

ambiguity-handling.comment: LL(1) conflicts are reported by the generator / language server; the restricted `/` ordered-choice operator provides PEG-style first-match where explicitly used. Semantic predicates and assertions handle context-sensitive disambiguation (e.g. C typedef names).

backtracking.comment: Backtracking only inside the restricted ordered choice `/` (parser state snapshot/restore); the `~` commit operator cuts further backtracking. Plain LL(1) alternatives are deterministic.

lexer-integration.comment: Pairs with logos by default (generated lexer.rs skeleton uses `#[derive(Logos)]`) but the README says this is not mandatory: the `ParserCallbacks::create_tokens` hook returns `(Vec<Token>, Vec<Span>)` from any source.

precedence-pratt-support.comment: Pratt parsing introduced in 0.7.0; precedence from alternative order in left-recursive rules, associativity via `right` declarations.

unicode-aware.comment: Not applicable at the parser level: the generated parser operates on a token vector with byte-range spans over `&str`; character handling is delegated to the lexer (logos by default). No Unicode statement in the docs.

input-types.comment: `Parser::new(source: &str, &mut diags)`; the user's `create_tokens` callback turns the `&str` into tokens + spans, so the effective parse input is a token vector produced from a string.

streaming-partial-input.comment: Full tokenization precedes parsing; no incomplete-input signalling.

zero-copy.comment: CST stores only `Range<usize>` spans and node tags; text is obtained by slicing the original `&'a str`.

span-tracking.comment: `Span = core::ops::Range<usize>` byte range; token spans stored directly, rule-node spans derived from contained tokens. Line/column comes from codespan-reporting at render time.

output-model.comment: Homogeneous lossless CST laid out linearly in a Vec (8-byte nodes); grammar operators for node rename (`@`), elision (`^`), markers and creation (`<1`, `1>name`) shape the tree.

semantic-actions.comment: AST is built by walking the CST afterwards. Grammar `actions`/`predicates`/`assertions` (`?1`, `!1`) call numbered methods on the user's `ParserCallbacks` impl for context-sensitive parsing, not for value construction.

whitespace-comment-handling.comment: `skip TokenName;` declarations make the parser ignore tokens while keeping them in the CST; the default lexer skeleton emits whitespace as tokens rather than dropping them.

stateful-parsing.comment: `ParserCallbacks::Context` associated type (0.10.0) threads user state; semantic actions/predicates use it e.g. for C typedef-name disambiguation in the C example.

error-recovery.comment: Recovery sets computed automatically from follow sets of grammar dominators (author's heuristic, inspired by matklad's resilient LL tutorial); strategies: skip expected token, advance with error node, break loop. No user configuration needed. README shows it producing meaningful trees where tree-sitter yields ERROR nodes.

multiple-errors-per-parse.comment: Diagnostics are accumulated in a `Vec<Diagnostic>` across the whole parse; an active-error-state mechanism suppresses cascades.

expected-token-reporting.comment: Generated messages read `invalid syntax, expected one of: '+', <Num>, ...` built by `syntax_error_message`.

custom-error-types.comment: `ParserCallbacks::Diagnostic` associated type + `create_diagnostic(span, message)`; skeleton defaults to `codespan_reporting::diagnostic::Diagnostic<()>` but any type works.

error-span-fidelity.comment: Every error carries a byte-range span; the generator supplies one primary span + message. Secondary labels are only possible if the user adds them in `create_diagnostic`.

diagnostic-crate-integration.comment: Skeleton and all examples use codespan-reporting by default (README: not mandatory).

contextual-error-messages.comment: No rule-labelling / custom-message facility in the grammar; syntax errors use the auto-generated expected-set message. Semantic assertions (`!n`) can emit user-written diagnostics for semantic checks only.

lossless-syntax-tree.comment: Lossless CST is a headline feature (the last 'L' in the name); skipped whitespace/comments are retained.

syntax-highlighting-queries.comment: No query language. `lelwel-ls` is an LSP for editing `.llw` grammar files, not for languages built with lelwel.

used-by-lsp-ide.comment: No major editor dependency found; reverse deps on lib.rs are small crates (fjord-schema, json_shape, yutu).

runtime-speed-tier.comment: No independent or reproducible benchmark found (README compares error resilience vs tree-sitter, not speed). Design is linear-time recursive descent with an 8-byte-node arena, but unmeasured.

compile-time-impact.comment: No measurements found. Generated code is plain recursive-descent functions (no deep generics / tables) plus a build.rs step; the default logos derive adds proc-macro cost.

allocation-strategy.comment: CST nodes are laid out linearly in a single `Vec<Node>` with a parallel `Vec<Span>`; no per-node heap allocation.

generated-code-size.comment: Emits one readable Rust function per rule plus a fixed runtime skeleton; no parse tables. Not measured in bytes.

no-std-support.comment: Generated runtime uses `Vec`/`String` and codespan-reporting; no `no_std`/`alloc` feature is documented.

msrv.comment: No `rust-version` in Cargo.toml; CI builds with the default stable toolchain only.

unsafe-usage.comment: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in lib.rs; no unsafe in the generated runtime skeleton.

proc-macro-reliance.comment: lelwel itself uses build.rs codegen, no proc-macros. The default lexer skeleton uses logos' derive macro, but README states logos is not mandatory.

dependency-count.comment: Generator crate (build-dependency): logos, codespan-reporting, rustc-hash (+ optional cli/lsp/wasm deps). There is no separate runtime crate; the generated code is self-contained and the user's crate adds logos + codespan-reporting by default (both replaceable).

wasm-compatible.comment: Crate has a `wasm` feature (wasm-bindgen) exposing `generate_syntax_tree`/`get_location`, so the generator itself is built for wasm32; generated parsers are pure Rust with no I/O. Not tested in CI.

async-friendly.comment: Parser and CST are plain `Vec`-based structs borrowing `&str` (likely `Send`), but nothing is documented and the parse is synchronous over a complete string.

maintenance-status.comment: Four releases Nov 2025–Apr 2026; last push 2026-08-22; 12 open issues (checked 2026-09-19).

documentation-quality.comment: docs.rs covers ~12% of items with no crate-level guide; the README grammar reference plus ten example grammars (C, Lua, WGSL, Python 2.7, JSON, TOML, ...) carry the documentation.

tutorial-book.comment: README quickstart only; no book or long-form tutorial.

notable-users.comment: Only 3 direct dependents on crates.io (fjord-schema, json_shape, yutu), none well-known.

bus-factor.comment: 0x2a-42 has 298 of ~304 commits; five other contributors with 1–2 commits each.
